messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Var Context Return Types
parts:
In trying to refactor everything I’ve realized that the current var_context
implementation is awkward because it’s sort of in the middle of two
functionalities. On one hand you could imagine the var_context just
returning an unstructured array of values corresponding to a variable
name, and on the other you could imagine the var_context returning
a properly formatted type. For example, calling

Eigen::VectorXd v = context.get_vals_r(“vector_name”);

would be incredibly useful to the internal code.

But right now var_context does something in between. It returns
a set of unstructured values but does know something about its
structure which is partially validated (namely the dims). This then
requires that the client know what type to be expecting, which is
fine for the generator but not for user-facing code.

Is there a pattern that would allow us to implement dynamic return types?
I can imagine metaprograms that properly map a block of vector data
in the var_context into the appropriate output (instead of having a dims
vector we’d have a type class which would not only contain the dim
information but also the type information) but I don’t see how we could
get dynamic return types with a single function signature.

Or should the user have to specify the type for validation? i.e.

template <typename T>
T var_context::get_vars_r(std::string& name) {
if (! contains_r(name))
throw unknown variable exception;
if (! T == type(name) )
throw type mismatch exception;

return convert<T>(vals_r(name);
}

In this case, how could the types be checked for equality dynamically?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Var Context Return Types
parts:
What about keeping the contract between the client interface (RStan,
PyStan, etc.) and Stan as simple as possible? Could one allow Stan to
pass error messages if something goes wrong? Perhaps we could just reuse
here whatever pattern we're going to use with error handling for the
sampler arguments?

(Why can't one use functions like `contains_r_only` to check types?)

Best,

-a

p.s. "client interface" is a reasonable generic term for RStan, PyStan,
etc., right?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Var Context Return Types
parts:
On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 5:27:54 AM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
Is there a pattern that would allow us to implement dynamic return types?
I can imagine metaprograms that properly map a block of vector data
in the var_context into the appropriate output (instead of having a dims
vector we’d have a type class which would not only contain the dim
information but also the type information) but I don’t see how we could
get dynamic return types with a single function signature.

Assuming C++11 in the future, we could store output in an Eigen::Tensor

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox-devel/unsupported/classEigen_1_1Tensor.html#details

whose template parameter only requires the number of dimensions.

So, if the Eigen::Tensor in the var_context were set up with the correct dimensions and the function reading it knew how many dimensions to expect, then it could just extract it when necessary and query its .dimensions(). But if we are assuming C++11, then wouldn't

auto v = context.get_vals_r("vector_name");

work also?

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Var Context Return Types
parts:
On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 6:14:01 PM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
If D were known at compile time, sure.  But we read in data/inits/etc dynamically.

The values and the dimensions of the data, inits, samples, ... are dynamic but stanc could be capable of substituting a number for D (the number of dimensions) in the C++ code given the .stan program. So if the .stan program is

data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  ...
}
parameters {
  matrix[N,K] theta;
}

and you need the initial values for theta or whatever the generated C++ code could read

Eigen::Tensor<double,2> theta_inits = var_context.inits("theta");

or I would think just auto if the compiler knows that var_context is holding an Eigen::Tensor<double,2>.

Ben

On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 5:35:44 PM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:

but depends on the dynamics argument.  

If context.get_vals_r("foo") were an Eigen::Tensor<double, D>, where D is known at compile time, regardless of that type of thing "foo" is in the .stan program, isn't that static enough for the compiler to infer?

I don't think we can assume C++11. We have too many legacy compilers
and systems like R that won't work with C++11 yet, so we're
going to trash a whole bunch of users if we assume C++11 any
time soon (by which I mean in the next year or more).

We don't need Eigen tensors, though --- we can just use something
like Boost arrays if we really need more generality.

- Bob
